teams.heading: Fiji's late scrum penalty lets Tommaso Allan kick Italy to 23-21 win
teams.body: Kitione Salawa had put Jake White's side ahead for the first time in Friday's 11th-place final at Twickenham, the No. 8's 55th-minute try and Caleb Muntz's third conversion making it 21-20 after Italy had led 17-0. The infringement came on the edge of Fiji's 22 with 13 minutes left; Allan, perfect with all five goal kicks, made no mistake. Fiji outscored the Azzurri three tries to two, a week after beating them 21-16 in Udine, but finish the Nations Championship 11th of 12.

lead.why: A new Fiji angle on Friday's defeat: the late scrum penalty that let Italy kick the winner after Salawa's try had put Fiji ahead.

teams.heading: Warburton hails Borthwick's 'stroke of genius' in resting Maro Itoje in July
teams.body: Writing in The Times, the former Lions captain credited Borthwick with suggesting the break that kept Itoje out of July's Southern Series Tests against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina. The 32-year-old lock has been 'on fire this autumn,' Warburton argued. He cited Itoje's 49 ruck entries in last Saturday's 37-12 win over the All Blacks, with Ollie Chessum next on 31. He also pointed to a team-high 19 tackles in 63 minutes against Japan. Itoje captains England again in today's third-place play-off at Twickenham.

lead.why: This is the only new England item. The selection news and the Starmer-Smith obituary have already run, and the doping row concerns South Africa and New Zealand.

teams.heading: Jean-Baptiste Gros shakes off injury doubt to make France bench against Springboks
teams.body: A doubt all week, Gros is named among France's replacements for the Nations Championship final at Twickenham. He is part of a 6-2 split alongside fellow prop Régis Montagne and hooker Peato Mauvaka, with Jefferson Poirot starting at loosehead. The prop had been set to face Argentina last weekend until he felt discomfort at the captain's run. Fabien Galthié insisted that naming him meant there was no uncertainty, while conceding that zero risk does not exist.

lead.why: It resolves the open Gros fitness thread: he is named on the bench for the final.

teams.heading: Andy Farrell hails Sam Prendergast's new authority after player-of-the-match Australia display
teams.body: The Leinster out-half, 23, started all four of Ireland's Nations Championship wins — over Argentina, Fiji, South Africa and Australia. He capped the month by kicking six from six off the tee in Friday's 38-14 defeat of the Wallabies and supplying the kick-pass for Rob Baloucoune's try. Farrell pointed to a change in his approach: "I think coming into camp I saw a shift in how he’s demanding of not just himself but of others as well." The head coach also credited extra pace built through hard pre-season work.

lead.why: Farrell's verdict on his first-choice out-half is new Ireland news, not a rerun of the already-reported result.

teams.heading: Italy's Tommaso Menoncello needs shoulder surgery and is a Six Nations doubt
teams.body: Toulouse said on Friday that the centre, hurt in training on Monday, will go under the knife next week for a recurring shoulder problem, likely ruling him out for three to four months. The 24-year-old joined the French champions this season as their sole recruit and has endured an injury-blighted campaign. He has been a cornerstone of Italy's upsurge under Gonzalo Quesada, and was named player of the tournament at the 2024 Six Nations.

lead.why: Fresh injury news on a key Italy player, and the Fiji win has already run.

teams.heading: Townsend makes 11 changes, with Darge back to captain Scotland against Argentina
teams.body: Only four starters survive the 67-5 rout of Japan: Darcy Graham, Jamie Dobie, Jonny Gray and Rory Hutchinson. Finn Russell is restored at fly-half for the seventh-place final at Twickenham. With Scotland's No. 8s injured, Magnus Bradbury starts there. "I'm sure he knows it's a big opportunity for him ahead of the Six Nations," Townsend said, adding he had considered hooker Seb Stephen for the back row before deciding against it this weekend.

teams.heading: Dafydd Jenkins reclaims Wales captaincy for Japan: 'I am definitely a different person'
teams.body: With Dewi Lake and Jac Morgan dropping to the bench as Steve Tandy rotates for Saturday's ninth-place final, the Exeter lock takes the armband more than two years after his baptism of fire as Warren Gatland's skipper in 2024, when Wales lost every Six Nations match. He was 21 then, the second-youngest Wales captain behind Sir Gareth Edwards, and now feels a lot more settled within the squad. Tandy called it "massive credit for him, so well-deserved." Jenkins wins his 35th cap.

lead.why: It is the only new Wales story: a change of captain for the Japan match, distinct from the Costelow and Morgan-Williams editions already run.

teams.heading: Contepomi picks uncapped Tobías Wade over Matías Moroni's 100th-cap chance
teams.body: The Zebre full-back takes the No. 23 shirt for Sunday's seventh-place final against Scotland at Twickenham and could make his Pumas debut off the bench. It leaves Moroni, added to the squad this week as cover for a group stripped by injury and suspension, stranded on 99 caps. The centre, who played at the 2015, 2019 and 2023 World Cups, would have become the second Argentina back to reach a century of Tests, after Nicolás Sánchez.

lead.why: A fresh Argentina selection call: an uncapped bench pick ahead of Moroni's chance at a 100th cap.

teams.heading: Max Jorgensen fails HIA after 29 minutes of Wallabies' loss to Ireland
teams.body: The bloodied wing had been strong in the air and a willing chaser before leaving Friday's 38-14 fifth-place play-off defeat at Allianz Stadium, Planet Rugby noted in rating him five. That exit came as Robert Baloucoune was causing problems on the other flank, scoring early in the second half when he collected a ball behind debutant James Ramm. Veteran Kurtley Beale, 37, replaced Jorgensen and finished the match on the wing.

lead.why: Max Jorgensen's failed HIA is a fresh injury development on Australia's own side, separate from the result already reported.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones hands Taufa Latu first Test start in Wales rematch
teams.body: Promoted from the bench after last week's 5-67 defeat by Scotland, Taufa Latu starts a Test for the first time, alongside Michael Stolberg and captain Warner Dearns in the second row, as Jones makes wholesale changes to his starting XV and matchday squad for the ninth-place final against Wales. Ryosuke Iwaihara and Seina Kimura were ruled out after the Scotland loss. The back row is unchanged, with Ben Gunter leading the competition on 11 dominant tackles and six jackals, while co-captain Naoto Saito is at scrumhalf.

teams.heading: BBC warns Rennie's All Blacks risk first six-defeat year since 1949
teams.body: Defeat by England in Saturday's Nations Championship finale would be New Zealand's sixth of the calendar year, Mike Henson writes for BBC Sport — a tally matched only once, in 1949, when a split squad played Test series in Australia and South Africa simultaneously. Their 2026 win percentage of 58.3% is already the third lowest of the professional era. Dave Rennie, who replaced the sacked Scott Robertson in March, presides over the most defeats in a calendar year since 1998, Planet Rugby notes.

lead.why: It is the freshest New Zealand item not already run, and it gives a concrete historical stake to the England rematch.

teams.heading: Manie Libbok starts at fly-half as Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu shifts to full-back
teams.body: Feinberg-Mngomezulu ran the show at No. 10 against Italy, France and Ireland, but makes way for the final against Les Bleus. Libbok came off the bench in the first two of those tests and then dropped out of the squad for the 20-17 defeat in Dublin. He now partners Cobus Reinach in the halves, with Ethan Hooker and Kurt-Lee Arendse completing the back three. The 29-year-old leans on an old understanding: "We gel nicely because we’ve played a lot together, even back at the DHL Stormers," said Libbok.

lead.why: A fresh Springbok selection call for the final, moving the first-choice fly-half to full-back to fit Libbok in, is the newest South Africa event and the ban story has already run.
